html:
From the 1520s the Oromo, a Cushitic-speaking people of herders and farmers from the south of the Ethiopian highlands, spread north and east over large parts of what is now Ethiopia.

They moved into lands worn out by the long war between the Ethiopian Empire and the Adal Sultanate under Ahmad Gragn. Their gadaa system organised men into age grades, and each new grade led campaigns, which gave the movement a steady rhythm over generations.

By the 1600s Oromo groups lived from the edge of Harar in the east to the far west of the highlands. Some kept herding, others took up farming, Christianity or Islam, and married into older populations. Later Oromo states, such as the Gibe kingdoms, grew rich on trade. The Ethiopian monk Bahrey wrote an account of them in 1593. The Oromo are now the largest people in Ethiopia.
sum: From the 1520s the Oromo, a Cushitic-speaking people of herders and farmers from the south of the Ethiopian highlands, spread north and east over large parts of what is now Ethiopia.
